prompts: Edit target: supplied v2 optical bench illustration. Make a v3 design preview with TWO targeted changes, preserving the existing 16:9 canvas and navy fine-grain illustrated style. 1) Enlarge experimental objects noticeably again: foreground plane, concave and convex mirror face diameters about 1.4 times their present v2 diameter, identical overall physical size, placed around x34%,51%,68% with no overlap; maintain complete rims and short stems inside frame, close to tabletop foreground. They should be large, prominent, easy to inspect, dominating the lower central third. Enlarge the empty right-side universal clamp opening another 1.4 times to fit these bigger mirror inserts. Enlarge the laser glowing exit aperture and front barrel another 1.4 times; grow housing proportionately but keep the rail carriage and posts rigid and plausibly scaled. Laser aperture center and clamp center must align on one horizontal axis, keeping a wide visible yellow light path. Maintain existing horizontal rail and tabletop horizon, no stretched hardware and no extra equipment. 2) On the LEFT LOWER open graph-paper notebook replace the existing incomplete shapes with TWO clear but subtle graphite pencil optics ray diagrams, drawn in the page perspective: upper diagram a concave mirror in side section, principal axis, three parallel incoming rays reflected to one focal point, tiny directional arrowheads; lower diagram a convex mirror, parallel incoming rays reflected divergently back toward source, fine dashed backward extensions meeting at a virtual focal point behind mirror. They must look like actual hand-drawn student study sketches on squared paper, thin desaturated graphite lines, no glowing rays, no readable text, no formulas. Keep the wooden pencil, eraser and right notebook unchanged. Preserve upper-left negative space for future heading, grid wall, soft vignette, matte paper/metal grain and restrained silver-blue reflections. No UI, captions, new labels, circles on background, buttons, sliders, people, photographic lighting or green laser. This is a preview only, not live webpage.

Edit ONLY the tiny graphite optics sketches on the bottom-left graph-paper notebook. Preserve ALL other pixels/composition: enlarged mirrors, laser, clamp, rail, lighting, textures, stationery, grid and 16:9 framing. Notebook should show two understated but physically correct pencil diagrams. Upper diagram: reflecting concave mirror positioned on RIGHT of its diagram, opening toward LEFT like a ')' curve; THREE horizontal incident rays travel LEFT-to-RIGHT toward mirror, and reflect RIGHT-to-LEFT, converging at a real focus on the LEFT of the mirror. Thus focal crossing and solid reflected rays must be on SAME LEFT side as incident rays, never to right behind mirror. Lower diagram: convex mirror positioned near center-right of diagram, bulging toward LEFT like '('; THREE parallel rays LEFT-to-RIGHT hit it, reflected solid rays diverge back toward LEFT; dashed reverse extensions go RIGHT behind mirror and meet a virtual point on RIGHT. Small arrowheads distinguish opposite propagation direction. Thin pale graphite lines, no writing, no formulas, perspective aligned with notebook page. No changes anywhere outside notebook sketches.
